title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a Riemann surface (or smooth complex curve). E_X is the sheaf of local coordinates, i.e. local holomorphic f with f' ≠ 0. E*_X is the sheaf of 'multiplicative' coordinates: nowhere-vanishing f with df/f nowhere zero, obtained from E_X by exp. Subgroups H of PGL(2,C) = GP(1,C) act on E_X by post-composition. The page identifies each quotient sheaf E_X/H(C), the sheaf of H-structures in the Ehresmann–Thurston (G,X)-sense, with a classical sheaf, and computes the corresponding 'écarts' (difference cocycles) between two coordinates f and g.

(1) H = G_a (translations). The map f ↦ df gives E_X/G_a(C) ≅ ω^{1*}_X, nowhere-vanishing 1-forms, an O*_X-torsor. The écart additif is Ecad(f,g) = dg/df = g'/f' ∈ Γ(O*_X).

(2) H = μ_n·G_a. The map f ↦ (df)^n gives E_X/(μ_n·G_a)(C) ≅ ω^{n*}_X. The écart is Ecaf_n = (g'/f')^n. The map α_n: φ ↦ φ^n passes from (1) to (2).

(3) H = G_m·G_a, the affine group. Affine structures correspond to connections on ω^1_X: f ↦ D_{df}, the connection making df horizontal. This gives E_X/Aff(C) ≅ Conn(ω^1_X), a torsor under ω^1_X. The écart affin is Ecaf(f,g) = D_{dg} − D_{df} = d(g'/f')/(g'/f') = (g''/g' − f''/f') dt, the pre-Schwarzian difference.
- The map β_n: ω^{n*} → Conn sends ω_n to the connection with ω_n^{1/n} horizontal.
- On O*_X it induces φ ↦ −(1/n) dφ/φ. Explicitly β_n(f dt^n) = D_{dt} − (1/n)(f'/f) dt; the page first writes +, then corrects.

(4) H = PGL(2,C). Projective structures form a torsor under ω^2_X (quadratic differentials): E_X/PGL2(C) ≅ Connproj(X), f ↦ c_pr(f).
- The écart projectif is Ecpr(f,g) = [(−2g'''/g' + 3(g''/g')²) − (same for f)] dt². This is −2 times the Schwarzian difference.
- The map γ: Conn(ω^1) → Connproj is γ(D+ω_1) = c_D + 2Dω_1 + ω_1², a Riccati/Miura-type quadratic map. In coordinates, γ(D_{dt} + f dt) = c_pr(t) + (2f' + f²) dt².
- Check: γβ_1(df) = c_pr(t) + (−2f'''/f' + 3(f''/f')²) dt² = c_pr(f). So the triangle E_X → ω^{1*} → Conn → Connproj commutes with the direct map f ↦ c_pr(f).
- In general γβ_n(f dt^n) = c_pr(t) + [−(2/n) f''/f + (2/n + 1/n²)(f'/f)²] dt². For n = 2 this is −f''/f + (5/4)(f'/f)², as written.

(5) Multiplicative side. The map f ↦ df/f gives E*_X/G_m(C) ≅ ω^{1*}_X.
- Quotienting further by the normalizer of the torus, N(T) = G_m ⋊ Z/2 (z ↦ cz, c/z; the page writes Z/nZ but means Z/2), gives E*_X/N(T)(C) ≅ ω^{2*}_X via (df/f)².
- Via exp, N(T)-structures correspond to half-translation structures (charts w ↦ ±w + b). This is the content of exp(±f + b) = e^b (exp f)^{±1}.
- The previous page's f + 1/f = h is the Z/2-invariant.

(6) The new map δ: ω^{2*}_X → Connproj(X) sends a nowhere-vanishing quadratic differential q to the projective structure of the exponential coordinate F with (dF/F)² = q. The page finds δ(q) = γβ_2(q) + q. Check, with ω_1 = f dt = dF/F: c_pr(F) = c_pr(t) + [f² − 2f''/f + 3(f'/f)²] dt² = γβ_1(ω_1) + ω_1². This is correct, and expresses that S(e^z) = −1/2 (with Grothendieck's −2S normalization, the extra term is +q).
- So the two projective structures attached to q differ exactly by q: the one from the flat coordinate ∫√q, and the one from the multiplicative coordinate exp∫√q.

Purpose. The page is a systematic dictionary of the 'analytic' structures (additive, n-differential, affine, multiplicative, half-translation, projective) on a curve, organised by the subgroup lattice of PGL2 and its compatibility diagram. It sits in a dossier on Gauss–Manin/Picard–Fuchs, where projective structures and Schwarzians arise from second-order Fuchsian equations. The previous page treats jets of Ω^{-1/2} and the matrix (Ω^0 Ω^{-1}; Ω^1 Ω^0), i.e. the sl2-oper picture.
errors: β_n first written with +(1/n) f'/f; the correct sign (consistent with φ ↦ −(1/n)dφ/φ at the top) is −(1/n) f'/f. Grothendieck's subsequent formula (−2f''/f + 3(f'/f)²) for n=1 is consistent with the minus sign, so the slip is self-corrected.

In δ(ω_2) = γβ_2(ω_2) + ω_2 = c_pr(t) + [−f''/f + (5/4)(f'/f)²] dt², the displayed bracket is only γβ_2(f dt²). The '+ω_2' term (+f dt²) is missing from the right-hand side, unless it is hidden in the scrawl.
The group written Z/nZ·G_m should be Z/2Z·G_m (the normalizer of the torus), as the map φ ↦ φ² and ω^{2*} show.
Normalization is non-standard but internally consistent: Ecpr = −2·(Schwarzian difference), matching γ(D+ω) = c_D + 2Dω + ω².

ideas.what: Sheaf-theoretic description of H-structures on a curve as quotients E_X/H(C) of the sheaf of local coordinates, for subgroups H ⊂ PGL2, each identified with a torsor (ω^{n*} under O*, Conn(ω^1) under ω^1, Connproj under ω^2)
ideas.modern_name: (G,X)-structures / special coordinate coverings; affine and projective connections on Riemann surfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ehresmann; Gunning (Lectures on Riemann Surfaces 1966, Special coordinate coverings 1967); Tyurin; later Thurston
ideas.where_published: Possibly echoed in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller / dessins discussion) only loosely

ideas.what: Écart affin (pre-Schwarzian, d log(g'/f')) and écart projectif (Schwarzian, normalized ×(−2)) as difference cocycles
ideas.modern_name: pre-Schwarzian and Schwarzian derivatives as 1- and 2-cocycles

ideas.what: Map from affine connections to projective structures γ(D+ω) = c_D + 2Dω + ω², and commutativity γ∘β_1∘d = c_pr
ideas.modern_name: Miura/Riccati map from sl2 connections (affine structures) to opers (projective structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Miura transform in this guise: Drinfeld–Sokolov, Frenkel

ideas.what: Half-translation (N(T)) structures via exp, and the map δ from nonvanishing quadratic differentials to projective structures through the multiplicative coordinate exp∫√q, with δ(q) = γβ_2(q) + q
ideas.modern_name: Projective structure of exp of the flat coordinate; Schwarzian of exp equals −1/2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical identity; folklore in flat-structure / projective-structure literature

missed.claim: A systematic diagram organising additive, n-differential, affine, multiplicative, half-translation and projective structures on a curve along the subgroup lattice of PGL2, with explicit compatibility maps (α_n, β_n, γ, δ). The mathematics is classical; the organised 'dictionary of écarts' in torsor language is a tidy unpublished exposition rather than a new result.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck in the 1970s working through Gunning-style projective/affine structures and oper-like jet bundles in the Picard–Fuchs context, before the Esquisse. No new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, carefully organised but classical material: Schwarzian and pre-Schwarzian cocycles, affine and projective structures as torsors, the Miura-type map, and the exp-coordinate projective structure of a quadratic differential. All of it is in Gunning and the later oper literature. The interest is mainly biographical/historical.
transcription_corrections: 'écart cadratif [?]' should read 'écart additif' (cf. Ecad below).
In the first line, 'd(dg/dt)' should be 'd(dg/df)'.
'δα'_2(ω_1) = γβ_2(ω_1) ω_1^2 = c_pr(t) + [−2f''/f + 3(f'/f)²]dt²' should read approximately 'δα'_2(ω_1) = γβ_1(ω_1) + ω_1² = c_pr(t) + [f² − 2f''/f + 3(f'/f)²]dt²'.
'exp(tf+b) = (exp b / c)(exp f)^{±1}' expresses exp(±f+b) = e^b (exp f)^{±1}, i.e. exp intertwining G_a⋊μ_2 with G_m⋊Z/2.
